name: SS&C Technologies Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: SS&C Technologies provides software and software-enabled services to the asset management, wealth, insurance, banking, and healthcare industries, including fund administration (SS&C GlobeOp), transfer agency and investor services (DST), Advent portfolio software, Calastone fund transaction network, Blue Prism intelligent automation, and healthcare claims and pharmacy administration. Founded in 1986 by CEO Bill Stone and headquartered in Windsor, Connecticut, it serves over 23,000 clients.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Over 70 acquisitions, including DST Systems ($5.4B), Advent, Blue Prism, and Calastone, have turned SS&C from a niche accounting software vendor into a $6.7B fintech and healthcare platform celebrating 40 years in 2026 [4][5]. AI Deployment (2/2): Under its 'Customer Zero' approach, SS&C ran 3,500 digital workers and 50 AI agents inside its own workflows by early 2026 with 300+ AI initiatives in development, and sells Blue Prism agentic automation to clients [3][4]. Market Share (1/2): SS&C is among the largest alternative fund administrators and transfer agents, but Q3 2026 adjusted organic growth of 5.2% points to steady rather than share-gaining momentum [1]. Pipeline (1/2): Bill Stone cites agentic AI and tokenization as next-generation offerings, without dated launch and revenue targets [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Development spending runs below pure-play software peers because much of revenue is labor-based outsourced services [5].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): SS&C's purpose of delivering technology and expertise that helps financial services and healthcare clients operate more efficiently is clear and industry-specific but describes what it does rather than a larger vision [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive, quantified foundation or community program was found beyond standard ESG reporting [6]. Employee Retention (1/2): Founder Bill Stone's 40-year tenure and Rahul Kanwar's internal promotion to President give unusual leadership continuity, though post-acquisition cost cutting tempers retention among acquired staff [3][5]. Insider Buying (0/2): No net open-market insider buying; Stone's pay was about 65% above the industry average in 2023 and say-on-pay failed in 2020 and 2022 [6][7].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Dividend stock (forced from portfolios.json) on all ten metrics (total weight 12). D/E of 113.1% scores 0.81; ROE of 12.4% scores 0.83; revenue growth of 7.8% YoY scores 0.93; 5yr revenue CAGR of 6.0% ($4.68B in 2020 to $6.27B in 2025) scores 0.74; Forward P/E of 10.37 scores 1.0; profit margin of 12.8% scores 0.64 [1][8]. Dividend metrics: payout ratio of 31.1% scores 1.0 (x1); 13 consecutive years paid (since 2014) scores 1.0 (x2); 10 consecutive years of growth (annual DPS up every year since 2017, including the Q3 2026 raise of 11.1% to $1.20) scores 1.0 (x1); and 5yr dividend CAGR of about 14.4% ($0.53 in 2020 to $1.04 in 2025) scores 1.0 (x2) [1][8]. Weighted sum 10.94/12 = 9.1, giving a score of 9. Liquidity floor cleared: 1.60M avg shares x $80.22 = $128M daily dollar volume [8].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): SS&C's regulated fund administration, transfer agency, and healthcare claims processing are protected by switching costs, audit and regulatory controls, and conservative clients, and Bill Stone calls AI a 'tailwind' behind a 'wide and deep moat' [3]. Still, software stocks sold off in 2026 over AI automation fears, and labor-heavy outsourced services face pricing pressure if clients or rivals automate the same work [3]. AI Opportunity (1/1): SS&C sells Blue Prism intelligent automation and agentic AI products to clients, an established AI-related revenue line acquired for about $1.6B in 2022 [3][4].

infinite_game.summary: Sinek would admire the 40-year founder continuity but question the game being played. SS&C's growth engine is debt-funded acquisition followed by cost extraction, with $7.5B of gross debt, 2.63x net leverage, and heavy buybacks ($154.8M in Q3 2026), a classic finite pattern [1]. The company endures, but through financial discipline rather than a cause.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): SS&C's purpose statements describe efficiency and client service in financial services and healthcare but do not describe a better future that employees would sacrifice for [4].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Stone made large, risky bets such as the $5.4B DST and Blue Prism acquisitions and is investing in agentic AI and tokenization, but these are capital-allocation bets funded by leverage rather than sacrifices of near-term earnings for a cause [1][5].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The playbook of buying businesses and cutting cost creates insecurity among acquired staff, and analysts flag the risk that cost cutting harms the expertise clients came for [3]. Repeated shareholder rejection of executive pay (2020, 2022) suggests a leader-centric culture [7].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): SS&C evolved from licensed software into outsourced services, healthcare administration, and intelligent automation, a meaningful but incremental, acquisition-led evolution [4][5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management's competitive language emphasizes its moat and taking share rather than learning from rivals [3].

investment_thesis: SS&C is a steady compounder priced like a value stock. Q3 2026 revenue rose 7.8% to $1,690.0M with 5.2% adjusted organic growth, adjusted EPS rose 14.8% to $1.78, and adjusted EBITDA reached a record $674.8M at a 39.9% margin [1]. Full-year guidance calls for $6,736-6,776M of adjusted revenue and $7.11-7.17 of adjusted EPS, and nine-month operating cash flow grew 10.4% to $1,216.3M [1]. At 10.4x forward earnings with a 31% payout ratio, an 11.1% dividend raise to $1.20, and steady buybacks, Infrastructure scores 9/10, and internal AI deployment (3,500 digital workers, 50 agents) supports margin expansion [1][3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is leverage, earnings quality, and AI pricing pressure. Gross debt is $7.5B (net leverage 2.63x), $2.0B of notes mature September 2027 and need refinancing, and GAAP Q3 EPS was flat at $0.83 with net income down 5.3% [1]. Organic growth of about 5% depends on labor-heavy services that AI could commoditize, which drove a software-sector selloff in 2026 [3]. Governance is a concern: say-on-pay failed in 2020 and 2022 and CEO pay ran about 65% above peers [6][7], while succession from the 40-year founder remains unresolved.
key_catalysts: Refinancing the $2.0B of September 2027 senior notes in Q4 2026 on favorable terms, removing a near-term overhang [1]
Q4 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.88-1.94 and continued EBITDA margin gains from internal AI agents and digital workers [1][3]
Commercial traction for agentic AI and tokenization offerings across the 23,000-client base [1][4]
key_risks: AI-driven pricing compression in labor-intensive fund administration and transfer agency services [3]
Leverage of 2.63x with $7.5B gross debt and acquisition integration risk if growth slows [1]
Founder-CEO succession and governance risk given Bill Stone's tenure and past failed say-on-pay votes [6][7]
